thread:
lee: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide the evaluation ordering semantics for smart routing. Do we go with a composable evaluator graph (nodes can short-circuit) or keep a linear pipeline with explicit priority tiers? Also: where do we draw cache + invalidation boundaries?

amanda: I still think a composable DAG gives us the most flexibility. Benefits: reuse evaluators (region, cost, latency, tier), we can short-circuit early when a high-priority constraint fails, and it's easier to instrument per-node.

raj: DAG is flexible but also more surprising runtime-wise. Main concern: evaluator cost adds CPU/latency. If evaluators are naive we could add tens of ms. Need strict O(1) fast checks for the hot path and ability to compile simple policies into an optimized fast path.

sam: Agreed with raj. We should define two modes: "fast-path" (precompiled, minimal checks) and "expressive-mode" (full DAG). By default route simple tenant workloads through fast-path.

olivia: Also: per-tenant overrides. We need a safe mechanism so customers can override e.g., region or model-tier, but only allowed keys and with audit trail. Overrides should be last-resort and TTL-bound.

lee: On cache boundaries — idea: cache decision fragments (e.g., region preference) at the edge, but keep final decision at central control-plane until we prove consistency. Risk: rollout changes and stale cache. Proposal: versioned cache keys including policy-config hash, tenant id, model id, and request-shape fingerprint.

raj: Versioned keys is good. Add an invalidation hook on policy deploy. Also: make cached entries short-lived (e.g., 30s) for dynamic signals (load/latency) and longer for static signals (region constraints).

amanda: Telemetry plan: emit events per evaluator execution with sampling; counters: evaluator_calls, evaluator_errors, decision_time_ms, cache_hits. This will let us detect slow evaluators and hotspots.

sam: Example minimal policy DSL sketch (for discussion):

```
policy "tenant_route" {
  when region == "eu" and tier != "dedicated" then prefer(region: eu, fallback: global)
  when observed_latency > 120ms then route(strategy: cost_optimized)
  else route(strategy: low_latency)
}
```

lee: I like that. We should also add explicit "short-circuit" keyword for safety e.g., `when x then short_circuit route(...)`. That ensures some evaluators can veto immediately.

olivia: From security/compliance side: UI + RBAC for policy editing. Only infra/product-approved users can deploy global policies; tenant-level overrides are gated. Audit logs mandatory.

raj: Testing notes: we need a policy-simulator harness that can run traffic sims and show decision distributions, latencies, and cost impact. Property tests for invariants (e.g., region constraint never broken, fallback always exists).

amanda: Migration plan sketch: 1) build evaluator library + stable API, 2) implement DAG runner but default to linear execution, 3) migrate a single simple policy to DAG (region preference) behind feature flag, 4) monitor metrics and rollout.

lee: Sounds good. Action items:
- amanda: draft proto API for evaluator library (due EOD Fri)
- raj: perf budget and microbench harness (due next Wed)
- sam: policy DSL toy parser + simulator (start this week)
- olivia: RBAC + audit requirements doc (sync with product)

sam: quick Q — where do we store policy configs? git-backed in control plane + CDN for edges?

lee: Store canonical configs in control-plane Git store (authoritative), push bundles to CDN/edge with signed configs and policy-hash for validation. Include invalidation hook on deploy.

infra-bot: deploybot: Rolling update for /services/routing-engine starting (canary 3%). See: https://deploys.redwood.internal/17648 :deploy: 

amanda: :thumbsup: on canary. We'll watch evaluator latency metrics.

raj: One more: compatibility with Dedicated/Private. Runtime API must be stable so private installs can opt-in. Keep implementation decoupled.

olivia: And add compliance checkbox for private installs (no outbound telemetry by default).

lee: Great discussion. I'll collate notes and update the RFC with proposed DAG runner, cache key format, and migration plan. Thanks all.

sam: +1

olivia: +1
